newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-GLASGOW RANGERS SLUMP TO FIRST LEAGUE DEFEAT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GLASGOW RANGERS SLUMP TO FIRST LEAGUE DEFEAT.

text.p: Scottish premier division champions Glasgow Rangers suffered a shock first league defeat of the season on Saturday when they crashed 2-1 to managerless Hibernian.
Scotland striker Darren Jackson and defender Graeme Donald hit goals in four second-half minutes for home side Hibernian to wipe out an opener from Jorg Albertz.
Goalkeeper Jim Leighton completed Hibernian's heroics by stopping a twice-taken 85th minute penalty kick from Brian Laudrup.
Laudrup's first effort had hit the bar but referee Stuart Dougal ordered a re-take with Andy Millen apparently having entered the penalty area.
Rangers stay top on 21 points, two clear of second-placed Celtic, with Aberdeen third on 14 and Hibernian, whose manager Alex Miller has quit after almost a decade in charge, in fourth place on 13.
Former Celtic contract rebel Pierre Van Hooydonk was their match-winner in a 1-0 home success against Motherwell.
Celtic, down to 10 men and struggling to break down a resolute defence, had their blushes spared by Van Hooydonk with a goal in the third minute of injury time.
The Dutch international, who appeared to be on his way out of the Glasgow club last week after rows with manager Tommy Burns, rose to head in a Jackie McNamara cross.
